set.sign_rules: Signs may be a maximum of 12 square feet, with a maximum of two signs per sale. Signs may not be placed on any public structure, including light poles, directional or stop signs, city right-of-way, or in street medians. Signs may be placed on a neighboring property with owner consent. All signs must be removed by 8:00 a.m. of the day following the completion of the sale.

racine-wi-rummage-sale-guide.notes: Racine Code Sec. 114-273(16) (Municode), accessory uses in the R1 single-family district only; other zoning districts were not checked. A rummage sale may last a maximum of three consecutive days per property, may start no earlier than 7:00 a.m., and may run no later than 6:00 p.m. Maximum of three sales within the calendar year, with a month separation between sales (recorded as 3 sales a year; the month-between-sales rule is also in these notes). Display is allowed within the property boundaries only; items for sale may not be placed within the sidewalk, parkway, alley, or street. Prohibited items at a rummage sale are motor vehicles and secondhand goods obtained for purposes of resale. Any person may file a complaint with the building inspection department. These sections do not mention a permit or fee, so those fields are left unknown.

jersey-city-nj-yard-sale-guide.notes: Jersey City Code Sec. 81-13(A)(3) (Municode). The owner, or lessee if the property is leased, of property used for a yard or garage sale is the person responsible for posting a handbill or sign advertising a yard or garage sale; the opened text frames that as the presumption used for sign-removal costs. This is recorded as a note only. No garage-sale permit, fee, duration, hours, or posting-location rules were taken from this section. Confidence stays unverified, and no legal fields are set.
